newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium calls for ceasefire in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Belgium calls for ceasefire in Zaire.

text.p: Belgium, the former colonial ruler of Zaire, on Wednesday called for a ceasefire in eastern Zaire and asked warring parties to grant aid groups access to refugees.

"We want priority to go to talks between the two sides, which must lead to a ceasefire, within the framework of a political solution," Belgian foreign ministry spokesman Andre Querton told reporters at a briefing.
"We insist on a ceasefire now," he added.
Rebels led by Laurent Kabila have captured a large part of eastern Zaire and are aiming to overthrow ailing Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko.
Kabila said earlier this month a ceasefire could only come after talks with the Zairean government about Mobutu stepping down.
A South African attempt to bring the two sides to the negotiating table has had little success.
Belgium urged the two sides to give aid organisations access to the many refugees in the area.

"It is necessary that aid organisations obtain access to the refugees in the east, in rebel territory. But aid workers should also get access to the population in the war zone from the west," Querton said.
Querton also said that the Belgian government has asked the 20 Belgians remaining in Kisangani to leave the eastern Zairean city.
Belgium does not have diplomatic contacts with Kabila.
Asked about the possibility that Belgium would join a multinational military force which would provide protection for relief organisations, Querton said that this would be highly unlikely.
